newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat police get suspended sentences after killing.
newsitem.headline: Croat police get suspended sentences after killing.

text.p: A Bosnian Croat court handed down suspended sentences to three Croat policemen on Thursday over an incident in which Croats shot dead a Moslem religious pilgrim and wounded 21.

A U.N. inquiry based on photographs taken of the violence found that Croat police in Mostar fired without provocation on Moslems trying to visit a cemetery on the Croat side of the ethnically divided Bosnian city on February 10.
The Croat court in west Mostar convicted three policemen of criminal mistreatment and overstepping their authority, the Croatian state news agency HINA reported.
The court acquitted two other Mostar Croat policemen of involvement in the attack, saying there was no hard proof.
HINA said defendant Zeljko Planinic, who was given a one-year suspended sentence, would be jailed only if he committed another criminal act within the next two years.
It said former west Mostar deputy police chief Ivan Hrkac and Bozo Peric were given six-month suspended terms and would be jailed only if they broke the law within a year.

About half a dozen Mostar Croat policemen were suspended over the attack, which stirred an international outcry and pressure for prosecution of the perpetrators and a crackdown on Croat nationalist gangsters who largely control the police.
One was west Mostar police chief Marko Radic, who was later replaced but is not known to have been charged.
Regional Bosnian Croat authorities also charged 11 Moslems with unspecified offences over the incident. The United Nations said there was no factual basis for such charges.

Hardline Croats declared a mini-state in Bosnia's Herzegovina region, including the west half of Mostar, during the 1992-95 Bosnian war and have refuse to merge it into a Moslem-Croat Federation as stipulated by the Dayton peace treaty.
